wu: Gadget Charades: students pick a tech word flashcard (phone, laptop, headphones) and act it out without speaking; classmates guess 'Is it a...?'
wuAlt: Tech Vocabulary Race: write 5 tech words on the board, students race to circle the correct one when you say it
Tech Survey: ask 3 classmates 'Do you like using...?' and tally yes/no answers
pres: Show real gadgets (phone, tablet, headphones) and model sentences: 'I like using my phone because it's fast'; 'I hate waiting for laptops to load'; check understanding with thumbs up/down for 'like/love/hate + -ing'
presAlt: Tech Poster Demo: display a poster with 5 tech facts, point and say 'This phone is cheaper than that one'; 'I love watching videos on tablets'
Dialogue Practice: read a short dialogue comparing phones, highlight 'like/hate + -ing' patterns
prac: Match the Gadget: students match device pictures to sentences like 'I love listening to music on...' in pairs; monitor and correct verb patterns
pracAlt: Tech Sentence Race: in teams, race to write sentences with 'like/love/hate + -ing' about gadgets; first team to write 5 correct sentences wins
Gadgets Survey: ask 5 classmates 'Do you like using...?' and record answers with tally marks
ls: Listen to a 1-minute debate: 'Phones vs Tablets for Students'; students circle 'phone' or 'tablet' based on who likes/dislikes each device; check answers in pairs
re: Tech Freeze Dance: play music with tech sounds (typing, notifications); when music stops, students freeze and say 'I love/hate using...' about a gadget
prod: Group Poster Project: in groups of 4, create a poster with 5 tech facts (e.g., 'Phones are cheaper than laptops', 'I love using tablets for games'); present to class with 'I like...' sentences
rw: Read a short text 'My Tech Habits' (40 words); answer 3 inference questions: 'Does the writer like phones? Why?', 'What device does the writer use most?', 'Why does the writer hate laptops?'
st: Watch a 2-minute animated story 'A Day Without Gadgets'; discuss 'What did you learn?'; end with 'Today we learned to describe gadgets—great work, goodbye!'
g: Teams race to write 3 comparative sentences about gadgets (e.g., 'Phones are smaller than laptops')
Students describe a gadget without saying its name (e.g., 'It's small, you call people')
Students write 'like/hate + -ing' sentences in bingo squares; cross off when classmates say them
Act out tech actions (typing, scrolling) for classmates to guess
Unscramble sentences like 'I love watching videos on tablets'
diff: Fast finishers: add 2 more comparisons to their poster (e.g., 'Tablets are heavier than phones')
Support: use sentence starters like 'I like... because...' on the poster
hw: Record a 1-minute video saying 3 tech facts (e.g., 'I love using phones for music')
Write 5 sentences comparing 2 gadgets (e.g., 'Laptops are bigger than phones')
Interview a family member about their tech habits and write 3 sentences
tip: Use local tech examples (e.g., 'In Morocco, many people use phones for payments') to make the lesson relatable and culturally relevant.
